text:
elena: FYI telemetry shows a small but steady spike in generation errors after the v2.1 rollout to prod canaries. Not an outage, but customer retries up.
sam: numbers? which cohorts?
elena: error_rate ~0.9% for long-context customers (seq>6000) over the last 2h. baseline ~0.04%.
sam: sounds like KV cache thrash / mem pressure on long sequences. saw something similar in the perf lab.
mike: quick mitigation idea: treat as a bug for impacted customers; hotfix = increase kv_timeout to 3s + sticky fallback to 2.0 for failing requests.
jordan: agree on a short-term config change. longer term this is an enhancement to eviction logic and batching heuristics.
anna: PM here94we need concrete decision rules. Proposal: if customer-facing error_rate >0.5% for >1h => classify as BUG and slot into current sprint for fix; else schedule as ENHANCEMENT next cycle.
nate: CS: we have 4 flagged orgs; two are enterprise with SLOs. they want immediate remediation, so leaning bug-first for those orgs.
opsbot: [deploy-bot] 1742012000 - Canary deploy 2.1.1 started -> rolling to 10% of canaries
sam: I can push hot config to the 4 orgs now and run a 30m AB check. Will report error_rate delta.
mike: also add a targeted canary that enables aggressive prefix caching and tighter batching for the long-context path.
jordan: grooming session tomorrow 10:30 PT, 25m. Invite infra, perf, cs, pm. Agenda: impact, repro steps, owner, rollback plan, cost delta.
anna: noted. I'll prepare customer impact notes and the backlog placement options (bug -> current sprint, enhancement -> next two sprints).
sam: I'll upload traces + replay script by EOD so infra can repro locally.
elena: thanks94if hotfix brings error_rate <0.3% and latency delta <5% we keep as mitigation + ship prioritized fix next sprint; otherwise escalate to platform upgrade and reprioritize scope. :thumbsup:
